headline: The Paris prosecutor opened an investigation on Nov 23; the hospital says no ransom has been demanded so far.
summary: Two new sources, both French: s005 RCI (Nov 23) and s006 Guadeloupe La 1ère (Nov 23, 10:17 PM Paris time). New c011 (Confirmed): the Paris prosecutor's cybercrime section opened an investigation on Nov 23, given to the national anti-cybercrime police office (RCI and La 1ère, separate outlets). New c012 (Reported, La 1ère): Orange Cyber Sécurité is on site with the national cybersecurity agency; full diagnosis expected at the end of the week. c008 updated: management says no ransom demand or contact so far; the director expects ransomware and a demand, which the hospital will not pay (label stays Not established). c009 updated: the hospital takes no position on a patient-data leak; diagnosis under way. Timeline t003. Re-read RCI s004 (updated Nov 23): gradual restart hoped for from the end of the week. La 1ère's Nov 23 summary says all of the hospital's data was encrypted; the director's own quotes do not say 'all', so c002 is unchanged. The pediatric move (c010) was not re-checked: no source read on whether it happened. No ANSSI, ARS or hospital statement found; no group claim found. q003 stays open. Head: known and two not_known lines updated. Not eligible for resolved.

headline: CHU de la Guadeloupe says it was hit by a cyberattack that encrypted data; Confirmed.
summary: New incident page. Sources read: RFI (relaying AFP and La 1ère), France-Antilles Guadeloupe, Guadeloupe La 1ère, RCI Guadeloupe (Tier 2, French). All four report the hospital director's statements, in separate interviews. Main question: Confirmed. Supplier entry: Reported (hedged). Ransom, data theft and group: Not established. A Le Parisien story was seen in search only and not read. No ANSSI or hospital notice read directly. Status monitoring. Privacy check done: no names, bylines, handles or contact details.
